summary: Poolside's mission is to close the gap between models and human intelligence by building proprietary models from scratch, combining next-token prediction with reinforcement learning—a thesis formed two and a half years ago. Their second-generation model, Malibu agent, was demonstrated live in VS Code, converting a government ADA codebase to Rust (approximately 1,152 lines), self-testing with bash commands, and adding an up-arrow command history feature using the rustyline library. The demo showcased live diff views, autonomous testing, and iterative bug-fixing. Poolside has spent the last year working in high-consequence code environments within government and defense sectors, where strict permissions and controlled agent behavior are essential. Beyond coding, their models handle broader knowledge work and are described as emotionally intelligent and capable of creative tasks like poem writing, though they don't emphasize those use cases. Compute has been the missing ingredient, now unlocked with over 40,000 GB300 GPUs coming online, enabling scaling to longer-horizon tasks. They envision agents progressing from hours-long to days-long autonomous work. A public release is planned for early next year via their own API and Amazon Bedrock, targeting both engineering assistant builders (Cursor, Windsurf, Replit) and application builders (Harvey, Writer). They are constructing a multi-gigawatt data center campus in West Texas and are actively seeking partners for reinforcement learning and fine-tuning on their models, from early checkpoints to current state. The founders, Jason Warner and Eiso Kant, first met in 2017 when Jason, then GitHub CTO, attempted to acquire Eiso's company, which had working code completion on LSTMs before the transformer architecture fully landed. Eiso declined, but they became close friends and eventually co-founded Poolside in 2022 after seeing ChatGPT and Anthropic emerge. Eiso initially resisted, suggesting they learn to paint and sail instead. They describe the current period as the awkward teenage years ahead of AGI, where the industry bridges the gap between raw intelligence and practical value. Their RL-plus-LLM thesis, once contrarian in the first 18 months, is now widely accepted as the field moves from completions to chat to agentic and increasingly autonomous approaches.

sections.title: Introduction and Poolside Mission
sections.summary: Jason Warner introduces Poolside's mission to close the gap between models and human intelligence by building models from scratch, combining next-token prediction with reinforcement learning. He introduces their second-generation model, Malibu agent.

sections.title: ADA to Rust Conversion Demo
sections.summary: Live demo in VS Code shows Poolside's agent analyzing an ADA codebase used in government satellites and converting it to Rust, writing approximately 1,152 lines of code. The agent self-tests with bash commands. Jason notes their work in high-consequence government and defense environments requiring strict permission controls.

sections.title: Demo Verification and Feature Addition
sections.summary: The team verifies the Rust conversion works, tests database operations, then asks the agent to add up-arrow command history cycling using the rustyline library. The agent identifies the package, modifies files, builds successfully, and writes its own test scripts.

sections.title: Platform Overview and Public Release Plans
sections.summary: Jason explains the VS Code demo is one interface into their platform; other interfaces include web and a downloadable agent. He notes broader knowledge work capabilities beyond coding. Public API release planned for early next year via their own API and Amazon Bedrock, targeting engineering assistant and application builders.

sections.title: Compute Scaling and Future Vision
sections.summary: Eiso discusses compute as the key bottleneck now unlocked with over 40,000 GB300 GPUs. He envisions agents progressing from hours-long to days-long tasks. They are building a multi-gigawatt data center campus in West Texas and seeking partners for RL and fine-tuning on their models.

sections.title: Founders' Origin Story and Closing Remarks
sections.summary: Jason recounts meeting Eiso in 2017 when, as GitHub CTO, he attempted to acquire Eiso's company that had working LSTM-based code completion before transformers fully landed. Eiso declined but they became close friends and later co-founded Poolside in 2022 after seeing ChatGPT and Anthropic emerge. Eiso initially resisted, suggesting painting and sailing instead. Eiso reflects that their RL-plus-LLM thesis was contrarian in the first 18 months but is now mainstream, and describes the current period as the awkward teenage years ahead of AGI where the industry bridges raw intelligence and practical value.
